subject: Close cadence: consolidated slippage tally & proposed escrow conditions
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Romero <natalie@brightwave.io>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Close cadence: consolidated slippage tally & proposed escrow conditions

Hi Natalie / team,

Thanks for the heads up on BrightWave's internal gating — appreciated. Per our conversation earlier, I want to capture the impact and propose a single-path plan to avoid ad hoc changes across the acceptance run.

Situation (short): BrightWave signaled a 2-week delay to the evaluation windows (integration + acceptance) driven by an additional security checklist and procurement batching. That pushes our originally targeted close date out by ~10 business days if we do no mitigation.

Why this matters: the delay increases risk to the professional services timeline and our capacity for the Dedicated pilot in Q3; we also have a second customer scheduled to onboard onto the same pool the week after your original go-live.

Proposed consolidated approach (attached MAP-v3.xlsx):
- Maintain the original acceptance criteria but split final acceptance into two short windows (canary + full).
- Offer a temporary two-week buffer in the MAP with gated acceptance (canary must pass basic throughput and data-flows).
- Conditional financial mitigation: 10% one-time usage credit applied to first invoice if BrightWave proceeds with the updated MAP and executes the SOW by the replenished procurement date.
- Escrow-like protection for both parties: if sign-off slips beyond the two-week buffer we move to an 'ownership hold' clause — Redwood will reserve Dedicated capacity for an additional 2 weeks and BrightWave will confirm revised procurement milestones; credit terms trigger if specific missed milestones occur.

Asks:
1) Can you confirm procurement's new target date by EOD tomorrow?
2) Accept the proposed two-week buffer + conditional credit?
3) If procurement needs a longer runway, let us know which milestone is the blocker so we can propose a staged mitigation.

I attached a redlined MAP (v3) for quick review. If we align, I’ll send a concise change-letter for signatures and copy procurement.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Sr. AM, Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0198

Attachment: MAP-v3.xlsx (mutual action plan draft — acceptance windows and credit term placeholders)
From: Natalie Romero <natalie@brightwave.io>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightWave Procurement <procurement@brightwave.io>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Close cadence: consolidated slippage tally & proposed escrow conditions

Mina, thanks for the clear note and the draft MAP.

We can confirm that the security team added a compliance walkthrough that will take approximately 7–10 business days to schedule and complete — that’s the primary driver. Procurement is leaning toward a 2-week window to finalize the PO but needs the SOW and clear credit language to move on the finance side.

Two quick clarifications:
- On the credit, procurement requires the attestation conditions (which exact milestones trigger the credit) and whether the credit is refundable or applied as a discount to the first invoice.
- For the escrow-like commitment, they want specific timing cutoffs and an explicit definition of 'canary pass' (e.g., 24h of steady-state throughput at X TPS and zero critical errors).

I attached our procurement intake; it lists the PO approvers and the vendor onboarding checklist. If you can produce a one-page addendum that enumerates milestone gates and credit trigger language, procurement can turn quickly.

If we can finalize that addendum and the SOW draft by Thu EOD, procurement thinks they can keep the target within the two-week buffer. Otherwise we’ll need to push the close ~3 weeks.

—Natalie
Natalie Romero
VP Product, BrightWave
Natalie@brightwave.io

Attachment: procurement-form.pdf
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: options on BrightWave slippage (analysis + recommended ask)

Mina / Rishi,

Quick internal note before we respond to procurement details:

Options (ranked by speed to close):
1) Accept two-week buffer + conditional 10% credit applied as a discount on first invoice (requires minimal legal redline). Provide a tight definition of canary pass (24h, 95th percentile latency < 250ms, no critical errors).
2) Offer two-week Dedicated trial (no charge) + engineering onboarding support (4x days) in lieu of a larger credit — helps them validate the canary quickly and keeps our unit economics intact.
3) If procurement insists on escrow/contractual hold for >2 weeks, escalate to Sales Leadership for a capacity reservation fee to cover the Dedicated blocking window.

Recommended path: combine options 1 + 2 — give the credit as discount AND include the one-time trial/eng support as a short-term operational concession. That gives BrightWave runway to validate and keeps us from over-committing headroom.

I attached a short redline on the SOW that calls out the canary definition and the credit trigger clause (SOW-diff-redlines.pdf). If Mina is aligned I suggest we send the one-page addendum and copy procurement.

Markus
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

Attachment: SOW-diff-redlines.pdf
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Romero <natalie@brightwave.io>, BrightWave Procurement <procurement@brightwave.io>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: amended MAP, credit & canary definitions — request for sign-off

Hi Natalie / Procurement team,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for sharing the procurement intake. Per internal review we’ve consolidated a final plan that should be workable for both sides. Summary below and the attached final MAP + credit-term draft.

Final consolidated plan (high level):
- MAP update: acceptance split into Canary Window (48 hours focused test) + Full Acceptance Window (48 hours). Canary window must satisfy: 24h of steady-state at >=50% of expected TPS with <=1% error rate on critical flows and 95th pctl latency < 250ms for those flows.
- Financial: 10% one-time usage credit applied as a discount to the first invoice if SOW is signed and the Canary Window is completed within the two-week buffer from procurement PO date. Credit automates; no refunds — discount on invoice.
- Operational: Redwood will provide a two-week Dedicated trial (no charge) and four days of onboarding support (remote) to accelerate the canary.
- Escrow clause: if procurement misses the two-week buffer and does not provide a confirmed PO date within that window, Redwood will reserve the Dedicated capacity for an additional two-week hold. If BrightWave elects to defer beyond that hold, the reserved capacity may convert to a paid reservation at a pre-agreed rate (details in Credit-term-draft.docx).

Next steps / asks:
1) Natalie / procurement — please confirm the PO target date and whether procurement needs any additional docs for finance (we included the one-page addendum in MAP-final.xlsx).
2) If agreed, procurement sends the DocuSign link for the SOW + one-page addendum and we will schedule a Thursday exec 30m to lock timelines.

We tried to balance time-to-validation for BrightWave with preserving Redwood’s capacity planning. Happy to work through any language changes — we just need procurement's PO target to keep the two-week buffer intact.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Sr. AM, Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0198

Attachments: MAP-final.xlsx, Credit-term-draft.docx
